anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: The system simultaneously experiences a Query Plan Selection Anomaly, in which the optimizer reuses or chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan despite accurate statistics, and a Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly, in which sessions block or spin while fighting for access to hot buffer pages, page pins, or latches inside the buffer manager.

Combined phenomena: The workload shows erratic plan flips, sudden shifts to full table scans or explosive nested-loop joins that dramatically raise page touches per statement. Concurrently, wait-event dashboards light up with buffer busy waits, page-latch or spinlock stalls, and CPU burn without matching throughput. I/O volumes surge because poorly chosen plans thrash the buffer pool, while latch contention lengthens critical sections, making individual statements slower and widening latency variance. Execution plans appear to deteriorate further under heavy concurrency, and end-to-end response times fluctuate unpredictably, obscuring whether the bottleneck is in execution logic or memory access.

Causal chain: Inefficient plans inflate logical I/O, repeatedly hammering a small set of root pages, index leaves, or temporary work tables, concentrating traffic on a handful of buffers and amplifying latch contention. The resulting stalls prolong statement runtimes and delay completion of data-modifying operations, which keeps those same hot pages pinned even longer, further escalating contention. Extended latch waits can, in turn, trigger automatic recompiles, plan cache evictions, or adaptive plan changes that pick yet another sub-optimal plan, creating a feedback loop. Together, the two root causes reinforce each other, driving up CPU spin, blocking time, and I/O pressure, and making the overall performance degradation deeper and harder to diagnose than either anomaly in isolation.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
